4.16.s:
“Na me diṭṭho ito pubbe, (iccāyasmā sāriputto)
Na suto uda kassaci;
Evaṁ vagguvado satthā,
Tusitā gaṇimāgato.
4.16.e:
“Never before have I seen,” said Venerable Sāriputta,
“or heard from anyone
about a teacher of such graceful speech,
come from Tusita heaven to lead a community.

4.16.s:
Sadevakassa lokassa,
yathā dissati cakkhumā;
Sabbaṁ tamaṁ vinodetvā,
ekova ratimajjhagā.
4.16.e:
To all the world with its gods
he appears as a Clear-eyed One
who has dispelled all darkness,
and alone attained to bliss.

4.16.s:
Taṁ buddhaṁ asitaṁ tādiṁ,
akuhaṁ gaṇimāgataṁ;
Bahūnamidha baddhānaṁ,
atthi pañhena āgamaṁ.
4.16.e:
On behalf of the many here still bound,
I have come seeking with a question
to that Buddha, unattached and impartial,
free of deceit, come to lead a community.

4.16.s:
Bhikkhuno vijigucchato,
bhajato rittamāsanaṁ;
Rukkhamūlaṁ susānaṁ vā,
pabbatānaṁ guhāsu vā.
4.16.e:
Suppose a mendicant who loathes attachment
frequents a lonely lodging—
the root of a tree, a charnel ground,
on mountains, or in caves.

4.16.s:
Uccāvacesu sayanesu,
kīvanto tattha bheravā;
Yehi bhikkhu na vedheyya,
nigghose sayanāsane.
4.16.e:
In these many different lodgings,
how many dangers are there
at which a mendicant in their silent lodging
ought not tremble?

4.16.s:
Katī parissayā loke,
gacchato agataṁ disaṁ;
Ye bhikkhu abhisambhave,
pantamhi sayanāsane.
4.16.e:
On their journey to the untrodden place,
how many adversities are there in the world
that must they overcome
in their remote lodging?

4.16.s:
Kyāssa byappathayo assu,
kyāssassu idha gocarā;
Kāni sīlabbatānāssu,
pahitattassa bhikkhuno.
4.16.e:
What ways of speech should they have?
Of what kind is their alms resort?
What precepts and vows
should a resolute mendicant uphold?

4.16.s:
Kaṁ so sikkhaṁ samādāya,
ekodi nipako sato;
Kammāro rajatasseva,
niddhame malamattano”.
4.16.e:
Having undertaken what training,
unified, alert, and mindful,
would they purge their own stains,
like a smith smelting silver?”

4.16.s:
“Vijigucchamānassa yadidaṁ phāsu, (sāriputtāti bhagavā)
Rittāsanaṁ sayanaṁ sevato ce;
Sambodhikāmassa yathānudhammaṁ,
Taṁ te pavakkhāmi yathā pajānaṁ.
4.16.e:
“If one who loathes attachment
frequents a lonely lodging,” said the Buddha to Sāriputta,
“in their search for awakening—
as accords with the teaching—
I shall tell you, as I understand it,
what is comfortable for them.

4.16.s:
Pañcannaṁ dhīro bhayānaṁ na bhāye,
Bhikkhu sato sapariyantacārī;
Ḍaṁsādhipātānaṁ sarīsapānaṁ,
Manussaphassānaṁ catuppadānaṁ.
4.16.e:
An attentive one, a mindful mendicant
living on the periphery
should not be afraid of five perils:
flies, mosquitoes, reptiles,
human contact, or four-legged creatures.

4.16.s:
Paradhammikānampi na santaseyya,
Disvāpi tesaṁ bahubheravāni;
Athāparāni abhisambhaveyya,
Parissayāni kusalānuesī.
4.16.e:
Nor should they fear followers of other teachings,
even having seen the many threats they pose.
And then one seeking the good
should overcome any other adversities.

4.16.s:
Ātaṅkaphassena khudāya phuṭṭho,
Sītaṁ athuṇhaṁ adhivāsayeyya;
So tehi phuṭṭho bahudhā anoko,
Viriyaṁ parakkammadaḷhaṁ kareyya.
4.16.e:
Afflicted by illness and hunger,
they should endure cold and excessive heat.
Though afflicted by many such things,
the homeless one
should exert energy, firmly striving.

4.16.s:
Theyyaṁ na kāre na musā bhaṇeyya,
Mettāya phasse tasathāvarāni;
Yadāvilattaṁ manaso vijaññā,
Kaṇhassa pakkhoti vinodayeyya.
4.16.e:
They must not steal or lie;
and should touch creatures firm or frail with love.
If they notice any clouding of the mind,
they should dispel it as Māra’s ally.

4.16.s:
Kodhātimānassa vasaṁ na gacche,
Mūlampi tesaṁ palikhañña tiṭṭhe;
Athappiyaṁ vā pana appiyaṁ vā,
Addhā bhavanto abhisambhaveyya.
4.16.e:
They must not fall under the sway
of anger or arrogance;
having dug them out by the root,
they would stand firm.
Then, faced with likes and dislikes,
they would surely overcome.

4.16.s:
Paññaṁ purakkhatvā kalyāṇapīti,
Vikkhambhaye tāni parissayāni;
Aratiṁ sahetha sayanamhi pante,
Caturo sahetha paridevadhamme.
4.16.e:
Putting wisdom in the foremost place,
rejoicing in goodness,
they would put an end to those adversities.
They’d vanquish discontent in their remote lodging.
And they’d vanquish the four lamentations:

4.16.s:
Kiṁsū asissāmi kuva vā asissaṁ,
Dukkhaṁ vata settha kvajja sessaṁ;
Ete vitakke paridevaneyye,
Vinayetha sekho aniketacārī.
4.16.e:
‘What will I eat? Where will I eat?
Oh, I slept badly! Where will I sleep?’
The trainee, the migrant without abode,
would dispel these lamentable thoughts.

4.16.s:
Annañca laddhā vasanañca kāle,
Mattaṁ so jaññā idha tosanatthaṁ;
So tesu gutto yatacāri gāme,
Rusitopi vācaṁ pharusaṁ na vajjā.
4.16.e:
Receiving food and clothes in due season,
they would know moderation
for the sake of contentment.
Guarded in these things,
walking restrained in the village,
they wouldn’t speak harshly even when provoked.

4.16.s:
Okkhittacakkhu na ca pādalolo,
Jhānānuyutto bahujāgarassa;
Upekkhamārabbha samāhitatto,
Takkāsayaṁ kukkucciyūpachinde.
4.16.e:
Eyes downcast, not footloose,
devoted to absorption, they’d be very wakeful.
Grounded in equanimity, serene,
they should cut off worrisome habits of thought.

4.16.s:
Cudito vacībhi satimābhinande,
Sabrahmacārīsu khilaṁ pabhinde;
Vācaṁ pamuñce kusalaṁ nātivelaṁ,
Janavādadhammāya na cetayeyya.
4.16.e:
A mindful one would welcome reproach,
and would dissolve hard-heartedness
toward their spiritual companions.
They may utter skillful speech, but not for too long,
and they shouldn’t provoke people to blame.

4.16.s:
Athāparaṁ pañca rajāni loke,
Yesaṁ satīmā vinayāya sikkhe;
Rūpesu saddesu atho rasesu,
Gandhesu phassesu sahetha rāgaṁ.
4.16.e:
And there are five more taints in the world,
for the removal of which
the mindful one should train,
vanquishing desire for sights,
sounds, flavors, smells, and touches.

4.16.s:
Etesu dhammesu vineyya chandaṁ,
Bhikkhu satimā suvimuttacitto;
Kālena so sammā dhammaṁ parivīmaṁsamāno,
Ekodibhūto vihane tamaṁ so”ti.
4.16.e:
Having removed desire for these things,
a mindful mendicant, their heart well freed,
rightly investigating the Dhamma in good time,
at one, would banish the darkness.”

5.1.s:
Kosalānaṁ purā rammā,
agamā dakkhiṇāpathaṁ;
Ākiñcaññaṁ patthayāno,
brāhmaṇo mantapāragū.
5.1.e:
From the fair city of the Kosalans
to the southern region
came a brahmin expert in hymns,
aspiring to nothingness.

5.1.s:
So assakassa visaye,
aḷakassa samāsane;
Vasi godhāvarīkūle,
uñchena ca phalena ca.
5.1.e:
He settled in a region under the shared dominion
of Assaka and Muḷaka,
where he lived on the bank of the Godāvarī River,
getting by on gleanings and fruit.

5.1.s:
Tasseva upanissāya,
gāmo ca vipulo ahu;
Tato jātena āyena,
mahāyaññamakappayi.
5.1.e:
He was supported
by a prosperous village nearby.
With the revenue earned from there
he performed a great sacrifice.

5.1.s:
Mahāyaññaṁ yajitvāna,
puna pāvisi assamaṁ;
Tasmiṁ paṭipaviṭṭhamhi,
añño āgañchi brāhmaṇo.
5.1.e:
When he had completed the great sacrifice,
he returned to his hermitage once more.
Upon his return,
another brahmin arrived.

5.1.s:
Ugghaṭṭapādo tasito,
paṅkadanto rajassiro;
So ca naṁ upasaṅkamma,
satāni pañca yācati.
5.1.e:
Foot-sore and thirsty,
with grotty teeth and dusty head,
he approached the other
and asked for five hundred coins.

5.1.s:
Tamenaṁ bāvarī disvā,
āsanena nimantayi;
Sukhañca kusalaṁ pucchi,
idaṁ vacanamabravi.
5.1.e:
When Bāvari saw him,
he invited him to sit down,
asked of his happiness and well-being,
and said the following.

5.1.s:
“Yaṁ kho mama deyyadhammaṁ,
Sabbaṁ visajjitaṁ mayā;
Anujānāhi me brahme,
Natthi pañcasatāni me”.
5.1.e:
“Whatever I had available to give,
I have already distributed.
Believe me, brahmin,
I don’t have five hundred coins.”

5.1.s:
“Sace me yācamānassa,
bhavaṁ nānupadassati;
Sattame divase tuyhaṁ,
muddhā phalatu sattadhā”.
5.1.e:
“If, good fellow, you do not
give me what I ask,
then on the seventh day,
let your head explode in seven!”

5.1.s:
Abhisaṅkharitvā kuhako,
bheravaṁ so akittayi;
Tassa taṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
bāvarī dukkhito ahu.
5.1.e:
After performing a ritual,
that charlatan uttered his dreadful curse.
When he heard these words,
Bāvari became distressed.

5.1.s:
Ussussati anāhāro,
Sokasallasamappito;
Athopi evaṁ cittassa,
Jhāne na ramatī mano.
5.1.e:
Not eating, he grew emaciated,
stricken by the dart of sorrow.
And in such a state of mind,
he could not enjoy absorption.

5.1.s:
Utrastaṁ dukkhitaṁ disvā,
Devatā atthakāminī;
Bāvariṁ upasaṅkamma,
Idaṁ vacanamabravi.
5.1.e:
Seeing him anxious and distraught,
a goddess wishing to help,
approached Bāvari
and said the following.

5.1.s:
“Na so muddhaṁ pajānāti,
Kuhako so dhanatthiko;
Muddhani muddhapāte vā,
Ñāṇaṁ tassa na vijjati”.
5.1.e:
“That charlatan understands nothing
about the head, he only wants money.
When it comes to heads or head-splitting,
he has no knowledge at all.”

5.1.s:
“Bhotī carahi jānāsi,
Taṁ me akkhāhi pucchitā;
Muddhaṁ muddhādhipātañca,
Taṁ suṇoma vaco tava”.
5.1.e:
“Then you, Madam, must know—
please answer my question.
Let me hear what you say
about heads and head-splitting.”

5.1.s:
“Ahampetaṁ na jānāmi,
Ñāṇamettha na vijjati;
Muddhani muddhādhipāte ca,
Jinānaṁ hettha dassanaṁ”.
5.1.e:
“I too do not know that,
I have no knowledge in that matter.
When it comes to heads or head-splitting,
it is the Victors who have vision.”

5.1.s:
“Atha ko carahi jānāti,
Asmiṁ pathavimaṇḍale;
Muddhaṁ muddhādhipātañca,
Taṁ me akkhāhi devate”.
5.1.e:
“So who then,
in all this vast territory,
does know about heads and head-splitting?
Please tell me, goddess.”

5.1.s:
“Purā kapilavatthumhā,
Nikkhanto lokanāyako;
Apacco okkākarājassa,
Sakyaputto pabhaṅkaro.
5.1.e:
“From the city of Kapilavatthu
the World Leader has gone forth.
He is a scion of King Okkāka,
a Sakyan, and a beacon.

5.1.s:
Buddho so bhagavā loke,
Dhammaṁ deseti cakkhumā;
Taṁ tvaṁ gantvāna pucchassu,
So te taṁ byākarissati”.
5.1.e:
That Buddha, the Blessed One in the world,
the Clear-eyed One, teaches Dhamma.
Go to him and ask—
he will answer you.”

5.1.s:
Sambuddhoti vaco sutvā,
Udaggo bāvarī ahu;
Sokassa tanuko āsi,
Pītiñca vipulaṁ labhi.
5.1.e:
When he heard the word “Buddha”,
Bāvari was elated.
His sorrow faded,
and he was filled to brimming with joy.

Uplifted, elated, and inspired,
Bāvari questioned that goddess:
“But in what village or town,
or in what land is the protector of the world,
where we may go and pay respects
to the Awakened One, best of men?”

5.1.s:
“Sāvatthiyaṁ kosalamandire jino,
Pahūtapañño varabhūrimedhaso;
So sakyaputto vidhuro anāsavo,
Muddhādhipātassa vidū narāsabho”.
5.1.e:
“Near Sāvatthī, home of the Kosalans,
is the Victor
abounding in wisdom, vast in intelligence.
That Sakyan is indefatigable, free of defilements,
that captain of men understands head-splitting.”

5.1.s:
Tato āmantayī sisse,
Brāhmaṇe mantapārage;
“Etha māṇavā akkhissaṁ,
Suṇātha vacanaṁ mama.
5.1.e:
Therefore he addressed his acolytes,
brahmins who had mastered the hymns:
“Come, students, I shall speak.
Listen to what I say.

Today has arisen in the world
one whose appearance in the world
is hard to find again—
he is renowned as the Awakened One.
Quickly go to Sāvatthī
and see the best of men.”

5.1.s:
“Kathaṁ carahi jānemu,
Disvā buddhoti brāhmaṇa;
Ajānataṁ no pabrūhi,
Yathā jānemu taṁ mayaṁ”.
5.1.e:
“Brahmin, how then are we to know
the Buddha when we see him?
We don’t know, please tell us,
so we can recognize him.”

5.1.s:
“Āgatāni hi mantesu,
Mahāpurisalakkhaṇā;
Dvattiṁsāni ca byākkhātā,
Samattā anupubbaso.
5.1.e:
“The marks of a great man
have been handed down in our hymns.
Thirty-two have been described,
complete and in order.

5.1.s:
Yassete honti gattesu,
Mahāpurisalakkhaṇā;
Dveyeva tassa gatiyo,
Tatiyā hi na vijjati.
5.1.e:
One upon whose body is found
these marks of a great man
has two possible destinies,
there is no third.

5.1.s:
Sace agāraṁ āvasati,
Vijeyya pathaviṁ imaṁ;
Adaṇḍena asatthena,
Dhammena manusāsati.
5.1.e:
If he stays at home,
having conquered this land
without rod or sword,
he shall govern by principle.

5.1.s:
Sace ca so pabbajati,
Agārā anagāriyaṁ;
Vivaṭṭacchado sambuddho,
Arahā bhavati anuttaro.
5.1.e:
But if he goes forth
from the lay life to homelessness,
he becomes an Awakened One, a perfected one,
with veil cast off, supreme.

5.1.s:
Jātiṁ gottañca lakkhaṇaṁ,
Mante sisse punāpare;
Muddhaṁ muddhādhipātañca,
Manasāyeva pucchatha.
5.1.e:
Ask him about my birth, clan, and marks,
my hymns and acolytes; and further,
about heads and head-splitting—
but do so only in your mind!

5.1.s:
Anāvaraṇadassāvī,
Yadi buddho bhavissati;
Manasā pucchite pañhe,
Vācāya vissajessati”.
5.1.e:
If he is the Buddha
of unhindered vision,
he will answer with his voice
the questions in your mind.”

5.1.s:
Bāvarissa vaco sutvā,
Sissā soḷasa brāhmaṇā;
Ajito tissametteyyo,
Puṇṇako atha mettagū.
5.1.e:
Sixteen brahmin acolytes
heard what Bāvari said:
Ajita, Tissametteyya,
Puṇṇaka and Mettagū,

5.1.s:
Dhotako upasīvo ca,
Nando ca atha hemako;
Todeyya-kappā dubhayo,
Jatukaṇṇī ca paṇḍito.
5.1.e:
Dhotaka and Upasīva,
Nanda and then Hemaka,
both Todeyya and Kappa,
and Jatukaṇṇī the astute,

5.1.s:
Bhadrāvudho udayo ca,
Posālo cāpi brāhmaṇo;
Mogharājā ca medhāvī,
Piṅgiyo ca mahāisi.
5.1.e:
Bhadrāvudha and Udaya,
and the brahmin Posāla,
Mogharāja the intelligent,
and Piṅgiya the great seer.

5.1.s:
Paccekagaṇino sabbe,
Sabbalokassa vissutā;
Jhāyī jhānaratā dhīrā,
Pubbavāsanavāsitā.
5.1.e:
Each of them had their own following,
they were renowned the whole world over.
Those attentive ones,
meditators who love absorption,
were redolent with the potential
of their past deeds.

5.1.s:
Bāvariṁ abhivādetvā,
Katvā ca naṁ padakkhiṇaṁ;
Jaṭājinadharā sabbe,
Pakkāmuṁ uttarāmukhā.
5.1.e:
Having bowed to Bāvari,
and circled him to his right,
they set out for the north,
with their dreadlocks and hides.

5.1.s:
Aḷakassa patiṭṭhānaṁ,
Purimāhissatiṁ tadā;
Ujjeniñcāpi gonaddhaṁ,
Vedisaṁ vanasavhayaṁ.
5.1.e:
First to Patiṭṭhāna of Muḷaka,
then on to the citadel of Māhissatī;
to Ujjenī and Gonaddhā,
and Vedisa, and Vanasa.

5.1.s:
Kosambiñcāpi sāketaṁ,
Sāvatthiñca puruttamaṁ;
Setabyaṁ kapilavatthuṁ,
Kusinārañca mandiraṁ.
5.1.e:
Then to Kosambī and Sāketa,
and the capital city of Sāvatthī;
on they went to Setavyā and Kapilavatthu,
and the homestead at Kusinārā.

5.1.s:
Pāvañca bhoganagaraṁ,
Vesāliṁ māgadhaṁ puraṁ;
Pāsāṇakaṁ cetiyañca,
Ramaṇīyaṁ manoramaṁ.
5.1.e:
To Pāvā they went, and Bhoga City,
and on to Vesālī and the Magadhan city.
Finally they reached the Pāsāṇaka Shrine,
fair and delightful.

5.1.s:
Tasitovudakaṁ sītaṁ,
Mahālābhaṁva vāṇijo;
Chāyaṁ ghammābhitattova,
Turitā pabbatamāruhuṁ.
5.1.e:
Like a thirsty person to cool water,
like a merchant to great profit,
like a heat-struck person to shade,
they quickly climbed the mountain.

5.1.s:
Bhagavā tamhi samaye,
Bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato;
Bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti,
Sīhova nadatī vane.
5.1.e:
At that time the Buddha,
at the fore of the mendicant Saṅgha,
was teaching the mendicants the Dhamma,
like a lion roaring in the jungle.

5.1.s:
Ajito addasa buddhaṁ,
Sataraṁsiṁva bhāṇumaṁ;
Candaṁ yathā pannarase,
Pāripūriṁ upāgataṁ.
5.1.e:
Ajita saw the Buddha,
like the sun shining with a hundred rays,
like the moon on the fifteenth day
when it has come into its fullness.

5.1.s:
Athassa gatte disvāna,
Paripūrañca byañjanaṁ;
Ekamantaṁ ṭhito haṭṭho,
Manopañhe apucchatha.
5.1.e:
Then he saw his body,
complete in all features.
Thrilled, he stood to one side
and asked this question in his mind.

5.1.s:
“Ādissa jammanaṁ brūhi,
Gottaṁ brūhi salakkhaṇaṁ;
Mantesu pāramiṁ brūhi,
Kati vāceti brāhmaṇo”.

“Vīsaṁ vassasataṁ āyu,
So ca gottena bāvarī;
Tīṇissa lakkhaṇā gatte,
Tiṇṇaṁ vedāna pāragū.
5.1.e:
“His age is a hundred and twenty.
By clan he is a Bāvari.
There are three marks on his body.
He is a master of the three Vedas,

5.1.s:
Lakkhaṇe itihāse ca,
Sanighaṇḍusakeṭubhe;
Pañcasatāni vāceti,
Sadhamme pāramiṁ gato”.
5.1.e:
the teachings on the marks, the testaments,
the vocabularies, and the rituals.
He teaches recitation to five hundred,
and has reached proficiency in his own teaching.”

5.1.s:
“Lakkhaṇānaṁ pavicayaṁ,
Bāvarissa naruttama;
Kaṅkhacchida pakāsehi,
Mā no kaṅkhāyitaṁ ahu”.
5.1.e:
“O supreme man, cutter of craving,
please reveal in detail
Bāvari’s marks—
let us doubt no longer!”

5.1.s:
“Mukhaṁ jivhāya chādeti,
Uṇṇassa bhamukantare;
Kosohitaṁ vatthaguyhaṁ,
Evaṁ jānāhi māṇava”.

Pucchañhi kiñci asuṇanto,
Sutvā pañhe viyākate;
Vicinteti jano sabbo,
Vedajāto katañjalī.
5.1.e:
Hearing the answers
without having heard any questions,
all the people, inspired,
with cupped palms, wondered:

5.1.s:
“Ko nu devo vā brahmā vā,
Indo vāpi sujampati;
Manasā pucchite pañhe,
Kametaṁ paṭibhāsati”.
5.1.e:
“Who is it that asked a question with their mind?
Was it a god or divinity?
Or Indra, Sujā’s husband?
To whom does the Buddha reply?”

5.1.s:
“Muddhaṁ muddhādhipātañca,
Bāvarī paripucchati;
Taṁ byākarohi bhagavā,
Kaṅkhaṁ vinaya no ise”.
5.1.e:
“Bāvari asks
about heads and head-splitting.
May the Buddha please answer,
and so, O seer, dispel our doubt.”

5.1.s:
“Avijjā muddhāti jānāhi,
Vijjā muddhādhipātinī;
Saddhāsatisamādhīhi,
Chandaviriyena saṁyutā”.
5.1.e:
“Know ignorance as the head,
and knowledge as the head-splitter,
when joined with faith, mindfulness, and immersion,
and enthusiasm and energy.”

5.1.s:
Tato vedena mahatā,
Santhambhitvāna māṇavo;
Ekaṁsaṁ ajinaṁ katvā,
Pādesu sirasā pati.
5.1.e:
At that, the student,
full of inspiration,
arranged his antelope-skin cloak over one shoulder,
and fell with his head to the Buddha’s feet.

5.1.s:
“Bāvarī brāhmaṇo bhoto,
Saha sissehi mārisa;
Udaggacitto sumano,
Pāde vandati cakkhuma”.
5.1.e:
“Good fellow, the brahmin Bāvari
together with his acolytes,
elated and happy,
bows to your feet, O Clear-eyed One!”

5.1.s:
“Sukhito bāvarī hotu,
Saha sissehi brāhmaṇo;
Tvañcāpi sukhito hohi,
Ciraṁ jīvāhi māṇava.
5.1.e:
“May the brahmin Bāvari be happy,
together with his acolytes.
And may you, too, be happy!
May you live long, student.

5.1.s:
Bāvarissa ca tuyhaṁ vā,
Sabbesaṁ sabbasaṁsayaṁ;
Katāvakāsā pucchavho,
Yaṁ kiñci manasicchatha”.
5.1.e:
To Bāvari and you all
I grant the opportunity to clear up all doubt.
Please ask
whatever you want.”

5.1.s:
Sambuddhena katokāso,
Nisīditvāna pañjalī;
Ajito paṭhamaṁ pañhaṁ,
Tattha pucchi tathāgataṁ.
5.1.e:
Granted the opportunity by the Buddha,
they sat down with cupped palms.
Ajita asked the Realized One
the first question right there.

5.2.s:
“Kenassu nivuto loko, (iccāyasmā ajito)
Kenassu nappakāsati;
Kissābhilepanaṁ brūsi,
Kiṁsu tassa mahabbhayaṁ”.
5.2.e:
“By what is the world shrouded?” said Venerable Ajita.
“Why does it not shine?
Tell me, what is its sullying?
What is its greatest fear?”

5.2.s:
“Avijjāya nivuto loko, (ajitāti bhagavā)
Vevicchā pamādā nappakāsati;
Jappābhilepanaṁ brūmi,
Dukkhamassa mahabbhayaṁ”.
5.2.e:
“The world is shrouded in ignorance.” replied the Buddha.
“Avarice and negligence make it not shine.
Muttered prayer is its sullying, I say.
Suffering is its greatest fear.”

5.2.s:
“Savanti sabbadhi sotā, (iccāyasmā ajito)
Sotānaṁ kiṁ nivāraṇaṁ;
Sotānaṁ saṁvaraṁ brūhi,
Kena sotā pidhiyyare”.
5.2.e:
“The streams flow everywhere,” said Venerable Ajita.
“What is there to block them?
And tell me the restraint of streams—
by what are they locked out?”

5.2.s:
“Yāni sotāni lokasmiṁ, (ajitāti bhagavā)
Sati tesaṁ nivāraṇaṁ;
Sotānaṁ saṁvaraṁ brūmi,
Paññāyete pidhiyyare”.
5.2.e:
“The streams in the world,” replied the Buddha,
“are blocked by mindfulness.
I tell you the restraint of streams—
they are locked out by wisdom.”

5.2.s:
“Paññā ceva sati yañca, (iccāyasmā ajito)
Nāmarūpañca mārisa;
Etaṁ me puṭṭho pabrūhi,
Katthetaṁ uparujjhati”.
5.2.e:
“That wisdom and mindfulness,” said Venerable Ajita,
“and that which is name and form, good fellow;
when questioned, please tell me of this:
where does this all cease?”

“This question which you have asked,
I shall answer you, Ajita.
Where name and form
cease with no residue left behind—
with the cessation of consciousness,
here they cease.”

5.2.s:
“Ye ca saṅkhātadhammāse,
ye ca sekhā puthū idha;
Tesaṁ me nipako iriyaṁ,
puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisa”.
5.2.e:
“There are those who have appraised the teaching,
and many kinds of trainees here.
Now you, being alert, are asked
to tell me their behavior, good fellow.”

5.2.s:
“Kāmesu nābhigijjheyya,
Manasānāvilo siyā;
Kusalo sabbadhammānaṁ,
Sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.
5.2.e:
“Not greedy for sensual pleasures,
their mind would be unclouded.
Skilled in all things,
a mendicant would wander mindful.”

5.3.e:
“Who here in the world is content?” said Venerable Tissametteyya.
“Who has no perturbations?
What thoughtful one, knowing both ends,
is not stuck in the middle?
Who do they say is a great man?
Who here has escaped the seamstress?”

5.3.s:
“Kāmesu brahmacariyavā, (metteyyāti bhagavā)
Vītataṇho sadā sato;
Saṅkhāya nibbuto bhikkhu,
Tassa no santi iñjitā.
5.3.e:
“Leading the spiritual life among sensual pleasures,” replied the Buddha,
“rid of craving, ever mindful;
a mendicant who, after appraisal, is quenched:
that’s who has no perturbations.

5.3.s:
So ubhantamabhiññāya,
Majjhe mantā na lippati;
Taṁ brūmi mahāpurisoti,
So idha sibbinimaccagā”ti.
5.3.e:
That thoughtful one, knowing both ends,
is not stuck in the middle.
He is a great man, I declare;
he has escaped the seamstress here.”

5.4.e:
“To the imperturbable, the seer of the root,” said Venerable Puṇṇaka,
“I have come seeking with a question.
On what grounds have seers and men,
aristocrats and brahmins here in the world
performed so many different
sacrifices to the gods?
I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this.”

“Whatever seers and men,” replied the Buddha,
“aristocrats and brahmins here in the world
have performed so many different
sacrifices to the gods:
all performed sacrifices bound to old age,
longing for this place.”

“As to those seers and men,” said Venerable Puṇṇaka,
“and aristocrats and brahmins here in the world
who have performed so many different
sacrifices to the gods:
being diligent in the technique of sacrifice,
have they crossed over rebirth and old age, good fellow?
I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this.”

5.4.s:
“Āsīsanti thomayanti abhijappanti juhanti, (puṇṇakāti bhagavā)
Kāmābhijappanti paṭicca lābhaṁ;
Te yājayogā bhavarāgarattā,
Nātariṁsu jātijaranti brūmi”.
5.4.e:
“Hoping, invoking, praying, and worshiping,” replied the Buddha,
“they pray for pleasure derived from profit.
Devoted to sacrifice, besotted by rebirth,
they’ve not crossed over rebirth and old age,
I declare.”

“If those devoted to sacrifice,” said Venerable Puṇṇaka,
“have not, by sacrificing,
crossed over rebirth and old age,
who then in the world of gods and humans
has crossed over rebirth and old age, good fellow?
I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this.”

5.4.s:
“Saṅkhāya lokasmi paroparāni, (puṇṇakāti bhagavā)
Yassiñjitaṁ natthi kuhiñci loke;
Santo vidhūmo anīgho nirāso,
Atāri so jātijaranti brūmī”ti.
5.4.e:
“Having appraised the world high and low,” replied the Buddha,
“there is nothing in the world that disturbs them.
Peaceful, unclouded, untroubled,
with no need for hope—
they’ve crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare.”

5.5.s:
“Pucchāmi taṁ bhagavā brūhi me taṁ, (iccāyasmā mettagū)
Maññāmi taṁ vedaguṁ bhāvitattaṁ;
Kuto nu dukkhā samudāgatā ime,
Ye keci lokasmimanekarūpā”.
5.5.e:
“I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this,” said Venerable Mettagū,
“for I think you are a knowledge master, evolved.
Where do all these sufferings come from,
in all their countless forms in the world?”

5.5.s:
“Dukkhassa ve maṁ pabhavaṁ apucchasi, (mettagūti bhagavā)
Taṁ te pavakkhāmi yathā pajānaṁ;
Upadhinidānā pabhavanti dukkhā,
Ye keci lokasmimanekarūpā.
5.5.e:
“You have rightly asked me of the origin of suffering,” replied the Buddha,
“I shall tell you as I understand it.
Attachment is the source of suffering
in all its countless forms in the world.

5.5.s:
Yo ve avidvā upadhiṁ karoti,
Punappunaṁ dukkhamupeti mando;
Tasmā pajānaṁ upadhiṁ na kayirā,
Dukkhassa jātippabhavānupassī”.
5.5.e:
When an ignorant person builds up attachments,
that dullard returns to suffering again and again.
So let one who understands
not build up attachments,
contemplating the inception of suffering and rebirth.”

“Whatever I asked you have explained to me.
I ask you once more, please tell me this:
How do the attentive cross the flood
of rebirth, old age, sorrow, and lamenting?
Please, sage, answer me clearly,
for truly you understand this matter.”

5.5.s:
“Kittayissāmi te dhammaṁ, (mettagūti bhagavā)
Diṭṭhe dhamme anītihaṁ;
Yaṁ viditvā sato caraṁ,
Tare loke visattikaṁ”.
5.5.e:
“I shall extol a teaching to you,” replied the Buddha,
“that is apparent in the present, not relying on legends.
Having understood it, one who lives mindfully
may cross over clinging in the world.”

5.5.s:
“Tañcāhaṁ abhinandāmi,
mahesi dhammamuttamaṁ;
Yaṁ viditvā sato caraṁ,
tare loke visattikaṁ”.
5.5.e:
“And I rejoice, great seer,
in that supreme teaching,
having understood which, one who lives mindfully
may cross over clinging in the world.”

5.5.s:
“Yaṁ kiñci sampajānāsi, (mettagūti bhagavā)
Uddhaṁ adho tiriyañcāpi majjhe;
Etesu nandiñca nivesanañca,
Panujja viññāṇaṁ bhave na tiṭṭhe.
5.5.e:
“Once you’ve expelled relishing and dogmatism,” replied the Buddha,
“regarding everything you are aware of—
above, below, all round, between—
having cast aside consciousness,
don’t continue in existence.

5.5.s:
Evaṁvihārī sato appamatto,
Bhikkhu caraṁ hitvā mamāyitāni;
Jātiṁ jaraṁ sokapariddavañca,
Idheva vidvā pajaheyya dukkhaṁ”.
5.5.e:
A mendicant who wanders meditating like this,
diligent and mindful, calling nothing their own,
would, being wise, give up the suffering
of rebirth, old age, sorrow and lamenting right here.”

5.5.s:
“Etābhinandāmi vaco mahesino,
Sukittitaṁ gotamanūpadhīkaṁ;
Addhā hi bhagavā pahāsi dukkhaṁ,
Tathā hi te vidito esa dhammo.
5.5.e:
“I rejoice in the words of the great seer!
You have expounded non-attachment well, Gotama.
Clearly the Buddha has given up suffering,
for truly you understand this matter.

5.5.s:
Te cāpi nūnappajaheyyu dukkhaṁ,
Ye tvaṁ muni aṭṭhitaṁ ovadeyya;
Taṁ taṁ namassāmi samecca nāga,
Appeva maṁ bhagavā aṭṭhitaṁ ovadeyya”.
5.5.e:
Surely, sage, those you’d regularly instruct
would also give up suffering.
Having met, I bow especially to you,
O spiritual giant;
hopefully the Buddha may regularly instruct me.”

5.5.s:
“Yaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ vedagumābhijaññā,
Akiñcanaṁ kāmabhave asattaṁ;
Addhā hi so oghamimaṁ atāri,
Tiṇṇo ca pāraṁ akhilo akaṅkho.
5.5.e:
“Any brahmin recognized as a knowledge master,
who has nothing, unattached to sensual life,
clearly has crossed this flood,
crossed to the far shore, kind, wishless.

5.5.s:
Vidvā ca yo vedagū naro idha,
Bhavābhave saṅgamimaṁ visajja;
So vītataṇho anīgho nirāso,
Atāri so jātijaranti brūmī”ti.
5.5.e:
And a wise person here, a knowledge master,
having untied the bond to life after life,
free of craving, untroubled, with no need for hope,
has crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare.”

5.6.s:
“Pucchāmi taṁ bhagavā brūhi metaṁ, (iccāyasmā dhotako)
Vācābhikaṅkhāmi mahesi tuyhaṁ;
Tava sutvāna nigghosaṁ,
Sikkhe nibbānamattano”.
5.6.e:
“I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this,” said Venerable Dhotaka,
“I long for your voice, great seer.
After hearing your message,
I shall train myself for extinguishment.”

5.6.s:
“Tenahātappaṁ karohi, (dhotakāti bhagavā)
Idheva nipako sato;
Ito sutvāna nigghosaṁ,
Sikkhe nibbānamattano”.
5.6.e:
“Well then, be keen, alert,” replied the Buddha,
“and mindful right here.
After hearing this message, go on
and train yourself for extinguishment.”

5.6.s:
“Passāmahaṁ devamanussaloke,
Akiñcanaṁ brāhmaṇamiriyamānaṁ;
Taṁ taṁ namassāmi samantacakkhu,
Pamuñca maṁ sakka kathaṅkathāhi”.
5.6.e:
“I see in the world of gods and humans
a brahmin traveling with nothing.
I bow especially to you, All-seer:
release me, Sakyan, from my indecisions.”

5.6.s:
“Nāhaṁ sahissāmi pamocanāya,
Kathaṅkathiṁ dhotaka kañci loke;
Dhammañca seṭṭhaṁ abhijānamāno,
Evaṁ tuvaṁ oghamimaṁ taresi”.
5.6.e:
“I am not able to release anyone
in the world who is indecisive, Dhotaka.
But when you understand the best of teachings,
you shall cross this flood.”

5.6.s:
“Anusāsa brahme karuṇāyamāno,
Vivekadhammaṁ yamahaṁ vijaññaṁ;
Yathāhaṁ ākāsova abyāpajjamāno,
Idheva santo asito careyyaṁ”.
5.6.e:
“Teach me, brahmin, out of compassion,
the principle of seclusion so that I may understand.
I wish to practice right here, peaceful, independent,
unobstructed as space itself.”

5.6.s:
“Kittayissāmi te santiṁ, (dhotakāti bhagavā)
Diṭṭhe dhamme anītihaṁ;
Yaṁ viditvā sato caraṁ,
Tare loke visattikaṁ”.
5.6.e:
“I shall extol that peace for you,” replied the Buddha,
“that is apparent in the present, not relying on legends.
Having understood it, one who lives mindfully
may cross over clinging in the world.”

5.6.s:
“Tañcāhaṁ abhinandāmi,
mahesi santimuttamaṁ;
Yaṁ viditvā sato caraṁ,
tare loke visattikaṁ”.
5.6.e:
“And I rejoice, great seer,
in that supreme peace,
having understood which, one who lives mindfully
may cross over clinging in the world.”

5.6.s:
“Yaṁ kiñci sampajānāsi, (dhotakāti bhagavā)
Uddhaṁ adho tiriyañcāpi majjhe;
Etaṁ viditvā saṅgoti loke,
Bhavābhavāya mākāsi taṇhan”ti.
5.6.e:
“Once you have understood that everything,” replied the Buddha,
“you are aware of in the world—
above, below, all round, between—
is a chain, don’t crave for life after life.”

5.7.s:
“Eko ahaṁ sakka mahantamoghaṁ, (iccāyasmā upasīvo)
Anissito no visahāmi tārituṁ;
Ārammaṇaṁ brūhi samantacakkhu,
Yaṁ nissito oghamimaṁ tareyyaṁ”.
5.7.e:
“Alone and independent, O Sakyan,” said Venerable Upasīva,
“I am not able to cross the great flood.
Tell me a support, All-seer,
depending on which I may cross this flood.”

5.7.s:
“Ākiñcaññaṁ pekkhamāno satimā, (upasīvāti bhagavā)
Natthīti nissāya tarassu oghaṁ;
Kāme pahāya virato kathāhi,
Taṇhakkhayaṁ nattamahābhipassa”.
5.7.e:
“Mindfully contemplating nothingness,” replied the Buddha,
“depending on the perception ‘there is nothing’,
cross the flood.
Giving up sensual pleasures,
refraining from chatter,
watch day and night for the ending of craving.”

5.7.s:
“Sabbesu kāmesu yo vītarāgo, (iccāyasmā upasīvo)
Ākiñcaññaṁ nissito hitvā maññaṁ;
Saññāvimokkhe parame vimutto,
Tiṭṭhe nu so tattha anānuyāyī”.
5.7.e:
“One who is free of desire for sensual pleasures,” said Venerable Upasīva,
“depending on nothingness, all else left behind,
freed in the ultimate liberation of perception:
might they remain there without traveling on?”

5.7.s:
“Sabbesu kāmesu yo vītarāgo, (upasīvāti bhagavā)
Ākiñcaññaṁ nissito hitvā maññaṁ;
Saññāvimokkhe parame vimutto,
Tiṭṭheyya so tattha anānuyāyī”.
5.7.e:
“One free of desire for sensual pleasures,” replied the Buddha,
“depending on nothingness, all else left behind,
freed in the ultimate liberation of perception:
they might remain there without traveling on.”

5.7.s:
“Tiṭṭhe ce so tattha anānuyāyī,
Pūgampi vassānaṁ samantacakkhu;
Tattheva so sītisiyā vimutto,
Cavetha viññāṇaṁ tathāvidhassa”.
5.7.e:
“If they were to remain there without traveling on,
even for myriad years, All-seer,
and, being freed, were to grow cool right there,
would the consciousness of that sort pass away?”

5.7.s:
“Accī yathā vātavegena khittā, (upasīvāti bhagavā)
Atthaṁ paleti na upeti saṅkhaṁ;
Evaṁ munī nāmakāyā vimutto,
Atthaṁ paleti na upeti saṅkhaṁ”.
5.7.e:
“As a flame tossed by a gust of wind,” replied the Buddha,
“comes to an end and cannot be reckoned;
so too, a sage freed
from the set of mental phenomena
comes to an end and cannot be reckoned.”

5.7.s:
“Atthaṅgato so uda vā so natthi,
Udāhu ve sassatiyā arogo;
Taṁ me munī sādhu viyākarohi,
Tathā hi te vidito esa dhammo”.
5.7.e:
“One who has disappeared—do they not exist?
Or are they free from disease for eternity?
Please, sage, answer me clearly,
for truly you understand this matter.”

5.7.s:
“Atthaṅgatassa na pamāṇamatthi, (upasīvāti bhagavā)
Yena naṁ vajjuṁ taṁ tassa natthi;
Sabbesu dhammesu samohatesu,
Samūhatā vādapathāpi sabbe”ti.
5.7.e:
“One who has disappeared cannot be defined,” replied the Buddha.
“They have nothing
by which others might describe them.
When all things have been eradicated,
eradicated, too, are all ways of speech.”

5.8.s:
“Santi loke munayo, (iccāyasmā nando)
Janā vadanti tayidaṁ kathaṁsu;
Ñāṇūpapannaṁ no muniṁ vadanti,
Udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannaṁ”.
5.8.e:
“People say there are sages in the world,” said Venerable Nanda,
“but how is this the case?
Is someone called a sage because of their knowledge,
or because of their way of life?”

5.8.s:
“Na diṭṭhiyā na sutiyā na ñāṇena, (…)
Munīdha nanda kusalā vadanti;
Visenikatvā anīghā nirāsā,
Caranti ye te munayoti brūmi”.
5.8.e:
“Experts do not speak of a sage in terms of
view, learning, or knowledge.
Those who are sages live far from the crowd, I say,
untroubled, with no need for hope.”

5.8.s:
“Ye kecime samaṇabrāhmaṇāse, (iccāyasmā nando)
Diṭṭhassutenāpi vadanti suddhiṁ;
Sīlabbatenāpi vadanti suddhiṁ,
Anekarūpena vadanti suddhiṁ.
Kaccissu te bhagavā tattha yatā carantā,
Atāru jātiñca jarañca mārisa;
Pucchāmi taṁ bhagavā brūhi me taṁ”.
5.8.e:
“As to those ascetics and brahmins,” said Venerable Nanda,
“who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard,
or in terms of precepts and vows,
or in terms of countless different things.
Living self-controlled in that matter,
have they crossed over rebirth and old age,
good fellow?
I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this.”

“As to those ascetics and brahmins,” replied the Buddha,
“who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard,
or in terms of precepts and vows,
or in terms of countless different things.
Even though they live self-controlled in that matter,
they’ve not crossed over rebirth and old age,
I declare.”

5.8.s:
“Ye kecime samaṇabrāhmaṇāse, (iccāyasmā nando)
Diṭṭhassutenāpi vadanti suddhiṁ;
Sīlabbatenāpi vadanti suddhiṁ,
Anekarūpena vadanti suddhiṁ.
Te ce muni brūsi anoghatiṇṇe,
Atha ko carahi devamanussaloke;
Atāri jātiñca jarañca mārisa,
Pucchāmi taṁ bhagavā brūhi me taṁ”.
5.8.e:
“As to those ascetics and brahmins,” said Venerable Nanda,
“who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard,
or in terms of precepts and vows,
or in terms of countless different things.
You say they have not crossed the flood, sage.
So who then in the world of gods and humans
has crossed over rebirth and old age, good fellow?
I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this.”

5.8.s:
“Nāhaṁ sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇāse, (nandāti bhagavā)
Jātijarāya nivutāti brūmi;
Ye sīdha diṭṭhaṁ va sutaṁ mutaṁ vā,
Sīlabbataṁ vāpi pahāya sabbaṁ.
Anekarūpampi pahāya sabbaṁ,
Taṇhaṁ pariññāya anāsavāse;
Te ve narā oghatiṇṇāti brūmi”.
5.8.e:
“I don’t say that all ascetics and brahmins,” replied the Buddha,
“are shrouded by rebirth and old age.
There are those here who have given up all
that is seen, heard, and thought,
and precepts and vows,
who have given up all the countless different things.
Fully understanding craving,
they are free of defilements,
those people, I say, have crossed the flood.”

5.8.s:
“Etābhinandāmi vaco mahesino,
Sukittitaṁ gotamanūpadhīkaṁ;
Ye sīdha diṭṭhaṁ va sutaṁ mutaṁ vā,
Sīlabbataṁ vāpi pahāya sabbaṁ.
Anekarūpampi pahāya sabbaṁ,
Taṇhaṁ pariññāya anāsavāse;
Ahampi te oghatiṇṇāti brūmī”ti.
5.8.e:
“I rejoice in the words of the great seer!
You have expounded non-attachment well, Gotama.
There are those here who have given up all
that is seen, heard, and thought,
and precepts and vows,
who have given up all the countless different things.
Fully understanding craving,
they are free of defilements,
those people, I agree, have crossed the flood.”

5.9.e:
“Those who have previously answered me,” said Venerable Hemaka,
“before Gotama’s teaching,
said ‘thus it was’ or ‘so it shall be’.
All that was just the testament of hearsay;
all that just fostered speculation:
I found no delight in that.

5.9.s:
Tvañca me dhammamakkhāhi,
taṇhānigghātanaṁ muni;
Yaṁ viditvā sato caraṁ,
tare loke visattikaṁ”.
5.9.e:
But you, sage, explain to me
the teaching that destroys craving.
Having understood it, one who lives mindfully
may cross over clinging in the world.”

“The removal of desire and lust, Hemaka,
for pleasant things
seen, heard, thought, or cognized here
is extinguishment, the state that does not pass.

5.9.s:
Etadaññāya ye satā,
Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā;
Upasantā ca te sadā,
Tiṇṇā loke visattikan”ti.
5.9.e:
Those who have fully understood this, mindful,
are quenched in this very life.
Always at peace,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

5.10.s:
“Yasmiṁ kāmā na vasanti, (iccāyasmā todeyyo)
Taṇhā yassa na vijjati;
Kathaṅkathā ca yo tiṇṇo,
Vimokkho tassa kīdiso”.
5.10.e:
“In whom sensual pleasures do not dwell,” said Venerable Todeyya,
“and for whom there is no craving,
and who has crossed over indecision—
of what kind is their liberation?”

5.10.s:
“Yasmiṁ kāmā na vasanti, (todeyyāti bhagavā)
Taṇhā yassa na vijjati;
Kathaṅkathā ca yo tiṇṇo,
Vimokkho tassa nāparo”.
5.10.e:
“In whom sensual pleasures do not dwell,” replied the Buddha,
“and for whom there is no craving,
and who has crossed over indecision—
there is no liberation that is further.”

5.10.s:
“Nirāsaso so uda āsasāno,
Paññāṇavā so uda paññakappī;
Muniṁ ahaṁ sakka yathā vijaññaṁ,
Taṁ me viyācikkha samantacakkhu”.
5.10.e:
“Are they free of hope,
or are they still in need of hope?
Do they possess wisdom,
or are they still forming wisdom?
O Sakyan, elucidate the sage to me,
so that I may understand, All-seer.”

5.10.s:
“Nirāsaso so na ca āsasāno,
Paññāṇavā so na ca paññakappī;
Evampi todeyya muniṁ vijāna,
Akiñcanaṁ kāmabhave asattan”ti.
5.10.e:
“They are free of hope,
they are not in need of hope.
They possess wisdom,
they are not still forming wisdom.
That, Todeyya, is how to understand a sage,
one who has nothing, unattached to sensual life.”

5.11.e:
“For those overwhelmed by old age and death,” said Venerable Kappa,
“stuck mid-stream
as the terrifying flood arises,
tell me an island, good fellow.
Explain to me an island
so this may occur no further.”

5.11.s:
“Majjhe sarasmiṁ tiṭṭhataṁ, (kappāti bhagavā)
Oghe jāte mahabbhaye;
Jarāmaccuparetānaṁ,
Dīpaṁ pabrūmi kappa te.
5.11.e:
“For those overwhelmed by old age and death,” replied the Buddha,
“stuck mid-stream
as the terrifying flood arises,
I shall tell you an island, Kappa.

5.11.s:
Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ,
etaṁ dīpaṁ anāparaṁ;
Nibbānaṁ iti naṁ brūmi,
jarāmaccuparikkhayaṁ.
5.11.e:
Having nothing, taking nothing:
this is the island with nothing further.
I call it extinguishment,
the ending of old age and death.

5.11.s:
Etadaññāya ye satā,
Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā;
Na te māravasānugā,
Na te mārassa paddhagū”ti.
5.11.e:
Those who have fully understood this, mindful,
are quenched in this very life.
They don’t fall under Māra’s sway,
nor are they his footmen.”

5.12.s:
“Sutvānahaṁ vīramakāmakāmiṁ, (iccāyasmā jatukaṇṇi)
Oghātigaṁ puṭṭhumakāmamāgamaṁ;
Santipadaṁ brūhi sahajanetta,
Yathātacchaṁ bhagavā brūhi metaṁ.
5.12.e:
“Hearing of the hero
with no desire for sensual pleasures,” said Venerable Jatukaṇṇī,
“who has passed over the flood, I’ve come
with a question for that desireless one.
Tell me the state of peace, O natural visionary.
Tell me this, Blessed One, as it really is.

For, having mastered sensual desires,
the Blessed One proceeds,
as the blazing sun shines on the earth.
May you of vast wisdom explain the teaching
to me of little wisdom so that I may understand
the giving up of rebirth and old age here.”

5.12.s:
“Kāmesu vinaya gedhaṁ, (jatukaṇṇīti bhagavā)
Nekkhammaṁ daṭṭhu khemato;
Uggahītaṁ nirattaṁ vā,
Mā te vijjittha kiñcanaṁ.
5.12.e:
“With desire for sensual pleasures dispelled,” replied the Buddha,
“seeing renunciation as sanctuary,
don’t be taking up or putting down
anything at all.

5.12.s:
Yaṁ pubbe taṁ visosehi,
pacchā te māhu kiñcanaṁ;
Majjhe ce no gahessasi,
upasanto carissasi.
5.12.e:
What came before, let wither away,
and after, let there be nothing.
If you don’t grasp at the middle,
you will live at peace.

5.12.s:
Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ,
Vītagedhassa brāhmaṇa;
Āsavāssa na vijjanti,
Yehi maccuvasaṁ vaje”ti.
5.12.e:
One rid of greed, brahmin,
for the whole realm of name and form,
has no defilements by which
they might fall under the sway of Death.”

5.13.s:
“Okañjahaṁ taṇhacchidaṁ anejaṁ, (iccāyasmā bhadrāvudho)
Nandiñjahaṁ oghatiṇṇaṁ vimuttaṁ;
Kappañjahaṁ abhiyāce sumedhaṁ,
Sutvāna nāgassa apanamissanti ito.
5.13.e:
“I beseech you, the bastion-leaver, the craving-cutter, the imperturbable,” said Venerable Bhadrāvudha,
“the delight-leaver, the flood-crosser, the freed,
the formulation-leaver, the intelligent.
Different people have gathered
from across the nations

5.13.s:
Nānājanā janapadehi saṅgatā,
Tava vīra vākyaṁ abhikaṅkhamānā;
Tesaṁ tuvaṁ sādhu viyākarohi,
Tathā hi te vidito esa dhammo”.
5.13.e:
wishing to hear your word, O hero.
After hearing the spiritual giant
they will depart from here.
Please, sage, answer them clearly,
for truly you understand this matter.”

5.13.s:
“Ādānataṇhaṁ vinayetha sabbaṁ, (bhadrāvudhāti bhagavā
Uddhaṁ adho tiriyañcāpi majjhe;
Yaṁ yañhi lokasmimupādiyanti,
Teneva māro anveti jantuṁ.
5.13.e:
“Dispel all craving for attachments,” replied the Buddha,
“above, below, all round, between.
For whatever a personage grasps in the world,
Māra pursues them right there.

5.13.s:
Tasmā pajānaṁ na upādiyetha,
Bhikkhu sato kiñcanaṁ sabbaloke;
Ādānasatte iti pekkhamāno,
Pajaṁ imaṁ maccudheyye visattan”ti.
5.13.e:
So let a mindful mendicant who understands
not grasp anything in all the world,
observing that, in clinging to attachments,
these people cling to the domain of death.”

5.14.e:
“To the meditator, rid of hopes,” said Venerable Udaya,
“who has completed the task, is free of defilements,
and has gone beyond all things,
I have come seeking with a question.
Tell me the liberation by enlightenment,
the smashing of ignorance.”

5.14.s:
“Pahānaṁ kāmacchandānaṁ, (udayāti bhagavā)
Domanassāna cūbhayaṁ;
Thinassa ca panūdanaṁ,
Kukkuccānaṁ nivāraṇaṁ.

Upekkhāsatisaṁsuddhaṁ,
dhammatakkapurejavaṁ;
Aññāvimokkhaṁ pabrūmi,
avijjāya pabhedanaṁ”.
5.14.e:
pure equanimity and mindfulness,
preceded by investigation of principles—
this, I declare, is liberation by enlightenment,
the smashing of ignorance.”

5.14.s:
“Kiṁsu saṁyojano loko,
kiṁsu tassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Kissassa vippahānena,
nibbānaṁ iti vuccati”.
5.14.e:
“What fetters the world?
How does it travel about?
With the giving up of what
is extinguishment spoken of?”

5.14.s:
“Nandisaṁyojano loko,
vitakkassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Taṇhāya vippahānena,
nibbānaṁ iti vuccati”.
5.14.e:
“Delight fetters the world.
It travels about by means of thought.
With the giving up of craving
extinguishment is spoken of.”

5.14.s:
“Kathaṁ satassa carato,
viññāṇaṁ uparujjhati;
Bhagavantaṁ puṭṭhumāgamma,
taṁ suṇoma vaco tava”.
5.14.e:
“For one living mindfully,
how does consciousness cease?
We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:
let us hear what you say.”

5.14.s:
“Ajjhattañca bahiddhā ca,
Vedanaṁ nābhinandato;
Evaṁ satassa carato,
Viññāṇaṁ uparujjhatī”ti.
5.14.e:
“Not taking pleasure in feeling
internally and externally—
for one living mindfully,
that’s how consciousness ceases.”

5.15.s:
“Yo atītaṁ ādisati, (iccāyasmā posālo)
Anejo chinnasaṁsayo;
Pāraguṁ sabbadhammānaṁ,
Atthi pañhena āgamaṁ.
5.15.e:
“To the one who reveals the past,” said Venerable Posāla,
“who is imperturbable, with doubts cut off,
and who has gone beyond all things,
I have come seeking with a question.

Consider one who perceives that form has vanished,
who has entirely given up the body,
and who sees nothing at all
internally and externally.
I ask the Sakyan about knowledge for them;
how should that sort be guided?”

5.15.s:
“Viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo sabbā, (posālāti bhagavā)
Abhijānaṁ tathāgato;
Tiṭṭhantamenaṁ jānāti,
Vimuttaṁ tapparāyaṇaṁ.
5.15.e:
“The Realized One directly knows,” said the Buddha,
“all planes of consciousness.
And he knows this one who remains,
committed to that as their final goal.

Understanding that desire for rebirth
in the dimension of nothingness is a fetter,
and directly knowing what this really means,
one then discerns that matter clearly.
That is their knowledge of truth,
the brahmin who has lived the life.”

5.16.s:
“Dvāhaṁ sakkaṁ apucchissaṁ, (iccāyasmā mogharājā)
Na me byākāsi cakkhumā;
Yāvatatiyañca devīsi,
Byākarotīti me sutaṁ.
5.16.e:
“Twice I have asked the Sakyan,” said Venerable Mogharāja,
“but you haven’t answered me, O Clear-eyed One.
I have heard that the divine seer
answers when questioned a third time.

5.16.s:
Ayaṁ loko paro loko,
brahmaloko sadevako;
Diṭṭhiṁ te nābhijānāti,
gotamassa yasassino.
5.16.e:
Regarding this world, the other world,
and the realm of divinity with its gods,
I’m not familiar with the view
of the renowned Gotama.

5.16.s:
Evaṁ abhikkantadassāviṁ,
atthi pañhena āgamaṁ;
Kathaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ,
maccurājā na passati”.
5.16.e:
So I have come seeking with a question
for the one of excellent vision.
How to look upon the world
so the King of Death won’t see you?”

“Look upon the world as empty,
Mogharāja, ever mindful.
Having uprooted the theory of self,
you may thus cross over death.
That’s how to look upon the world
so the King of Death won’t see you.”

5.17.e:
“I am old, feeble, and pallid,” said Venerable Piṅgiya,
“my eyes unclear, my hearing faint—
don’t let me perish while still confused.
Explain the teaching so that I may understand
the giving up of rebirth and old age here.”

5.17.s:
“Disvāna rūpesu vihaññamāne, (piṅgiyāti bhagavā)
Ruppanti rūpesu janā pamattā;
Tasmā tuvaṁ piṅgiya appamatto,
Jahassu rūpaṁ apunabbhavāya”.
5.17.e:
“Seeing them being harmed
on account of forms,” replied the Buddha,
“those negligent folk are inflicted
on account of forms—
therefore, Piṅgiya, being diligent,
give up form so as not to be reborn.”

“The four quarters, the intermediate directions,
below, and above: in these ten directions
there’s nothing at all in the world
that you’ve not seen, heard, thought, or cognized.
Explain the teaching so that I may understand
the giving up of rebirth and old age here.”

5.17.s:
“Taṇhādhipanne manuje pekkhamāno, (piṅgiyāti bhagavā)
Santāpajāte jarasā parete;
Tasmā tuvaṁ piṅgiya appamatto,
Jahassu taṇhaṁ apunabbhavāyā”ti.
5.17.e:
“Observing mankind sunk in craving,” replied the Buddha,
“tormented, mired in old age;
therefore, Piṅgiya, being diligent,
give up craving so as not to be reborn.”

5.18.s: Idamavoca bhagavā magadhesu viharanto pāsāṇake cetiye, paricārakasoḷasānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ ajjhiṭṭho puṭṭho puṭṭho pañhaṁ byākāsi. Ekamekassa cepi pañhassa atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammaṁ paṭipajjeyya, gaccheyyeva jarāmaraṇassa pāraṁ. Pāraṅgamanīyā ime dhammāti, tasmā imassa dhammapariyāyassa pārāyananteva adhivacanaṁ.
5.18.e: This was said by the Buddha while staying in the land of the Magadhans at the Pāsāṇaka Shrine. When requested by the sixteen brahmin devotees, he answered their questions one by one. If you understand the meaning and the teaching of each of these questions, and practice in line with the teaching, you may go right to the far shore of old age and death. These teachings are said to lead to the far shore, which is why the name of this exposition of the teaching is “The Way to the Far Shore”.
5.18.t: Homage to the Way to the Far Shore (Pārāyanatthutigāthā)

5.18.s:
Ajito tissametteyyo,
puṇṇako atha mettagū;
Dhotako upasīvo ca,
nando ca atha hemako.
5.18.e:
Ajita, Tissametteyya,
Puṇṇaka and Mettagū,
Dhotaka and Upasiva,
Nanda and then Hemaka,

both Todeyya and Kappa,
and Jatukaṇṇī the astute,
Bhadrāvudha and Udaya,
and the brahmin Posāla,
Mogharāja the intelligent,
and Piṅgiya the great seer:

5.18.s:
Ete buddhaṁ upāgacchuṁ,
sampannacaraṇaṁ isiṁ;
Pucchantā nipuṇe pañhe,
buddhaseṭṭhaṁ upāgamuṁ.
5.18.e:
they approached the Buddha,
the seer of consummate conduct.
Asking their subtle questions,
they came to the most excellent Buddha.

5.18.s:
Tesaṁ buddho pabyākāsi,
pañhe puṭṭho yathātathaṁ;
Pañhānaṁ veyyākaraṇena,
tosesi brāhmaṇe muni.
5.18.e:
The Buddha answered their questions
in accordance with truth.
The sage satisfied the brahmins
with his answers to their questions.

5.18.s:
Te tositā cakkhumatā,
buddhenādiccabandhunā;
Brahmacariyamacariṁsu,
varapaññassa santike.
5.18.e:
Those who were satisfied by the Clear-eyed One,
the Buddha, Kinsman of the Sun,
led the spiritual life in his presence,
the one of such outstanding wisdom.

5.18.s:
Ekamekassa pañhassa,
yathā buddhena desitaṁ;
Tathā yo paṭipajjeyya,
gacche pāraṁ apārato.
5.18.e:
If you practice in accordance
with each of these questions
as taught by the Buddha,
you’ll go from the near shore to the far.

5.18.s:
Apārā pāraṁ gaccheyya,
bhāvento maggamuttamaṁ;
Maggo so pāraṁ gamanāya,
tasmā pārāyanaṁ iti.
5.18.e:
Developing the supreme path,
you’ll go from the near shore to the far.
This path is for going to the far shore;
that’s why it’s called “The Way to the Far Shore”.

5.19.e:
“I shall keep reciting the Way to the Far Shore,” said Venerable Piṅgiya,
“which was taught as it was seen
by the immaculate one of vast intelligence.
He is desireless, unentangled, a spiritual giant:
why would he speak falsely?
5.19.t: Preserving the Way to the Far Shore (Pārāyanānugītigāthā)

5.19.s:
Pahīnamalamohassa,
mānamakkhappahāyino;
Handāhaṁ kittayissāmi,
giraṁ vaṇṇūpasañhitaṁ.
5.19.e:
Come, let me extol
in sweet words of praise
the one who’s given up stains and delusions,
conceit and contempt.

5.19.s:
Tamonudo buddho samantacakkhu,
Lokantagū sabbabhavātivatto;
Anāsavo sabbadukkhappahīno,
Saccavhayo brahme upāsito me.
5.19.e:
The Buddha, All-seer, dispeller of darkness,
has gone to world’s end, beyond all rebirths;
he is free of defilements,
and has given up all suffering,
the rightly-named one, brahmin, is revered by me.

5.19.s:
Dijo yathā kubbanakaṁ pahāya,
Bahupphalaṁ kānanamāvaseyya;
Evampahaṁ appadasse pahāya,
Mahodadhiṁ haṁsoriva ajjhapatto.
5.19.e:
Like a bird that flees a little copse,
to roost in a forest abounding in fruit,
I’ve left the near-sighted behind,
like a swan come to a great river.

Those who explained to me previously,
before Gotama’s teaching,
said ‘thus it was’ or ‘so it shall be’.
All that was just the testament of hearsay;
all that just fostered speculation.

5.19.s:
Eko tamanudāsino,
jutimā so pabhaṅkaro;
Gotamo bhūripaññāṇo,
gotamo bhūrimedhaso.
5.19.e:
Alone, the dispeller of darkness
is brilliant, a beacon:
Gotama, vast in wisdom,
Gotama, vast in intelligence.

5.19.s:
Yo me dhammamadesesi,
Sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṁ;
Taṇhakkhayamanītikaṁ,
Yassa natthi upamā kvaci”.
5.19.e:
He is the one who taught me Dhamma,
apparent in the present life, immediately effective,
the untroubled, the end of craving,
to which there is no compare.”

5.19.s:
“Kiṁ nu tamhā vippavasasi,
muhuttamapi piṅgiya;
Gotamā bhūripaññāṇā,
gotamā bhūrimedhasā.
5.19.e:
“Why would you dwell apart from him
even for an hour, Piṅgiya?
From Gotama, vast in wisdom,
from Gotama, vast in intelligence?

5.19.s:
Yo te dhammamadesesi,
Sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṁ;
Taṇhakkhayamanītikaṁ,
Yassa natthi upamā kvaci”.
5.19.e:
He is the one who taught you Dhamma,
apparent in the present life, immediately effective,
the untroubled, the end of craving,
to which there is no compare.”

5.19.s:
“Nāhaṁ tamhā vippavasāmi,
Muhuttamapi brāhmaṇa;
Gotamā bhūripaññāṇā,
Gotamā bhūrimedhasā.
5.19.e:
“I never dwell apart from him,
not even for an hour, brahmin.
From Gotama, vast in wisdom,
from Gotama, vast in intelligence.

5.19.s:
Yo me dhammamadesesi,
Sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṁ;
Taṇhakkhayamanītikaṁ,
Yassa natthi upamā kvaci.
5.19.e:
He is the one who taught me Dhamma,
apparent in the present life, immediately effective,
the untroubled, the end of craving,
to which there is no compare.

5.19.s:
Passāmi naṁ manasā cakkhunāva,
Rattindivaṁ brāhmaṇa appamatto;
Namassamāno vivasemi rattiṁ,
Teneva maññāmi avippavāsaṁ.
5.19.e:
Being diligent, I see him
in my mind’s eye day and night.
I spend the night in homage to him,
hence I think I dwell with him.

5.19.s:
Saddhā ca pīti ca mano sati ca,
Nāpentime gotamasāsanamhā;
Yaṁ yaṁ disaṁ vajati bhūripañño,
Sa tena teneva natohamasmi.
5.19.e:
My faith and joy and intent and mindfulness
never stray from Gotama’s teaching.
I bow to whatever direction
the one of vast wisdom heads.

5.19.s:
Jiṇṇassa me dubbalathāmakassa,
Teneva kāyo na paleti tattha;
Saṅkappayantāya vajāmi niccaṁ,
Mano hi me brāhmaṇa tena yutto.
5.19.e:
I’m old and feeble,
so my body cannot go there,
but I always travel in my thoughts,
for my mind, brahmin, is bound to him.

5.19.s:
Paṅke sayāno pariphandamāno,
Dīpā dīpaṁ upaplaviṁ;
Athaddasāsiṁ sambuddhaṁ,
Oghatiṇṇamanāsavaṁ”.
5.19.e:
Lying floundering in the mud,
I drifted from island to island.
Then I saw the Buddha,
the undefiled one who has crossed the flood.”

5.19.s:
“Yathā ahū vakkali muttasaddho,
Bhadrāvudho āḷavigotamo ca;
Evamevaṁ tvampi pamuñcassu saddhaṁ,
Gamissasi tvaṁ piṅgiya maccudheyyassa pāraṁ”.
5.19.e:
“Just as Vakkali was committed to faith—
Bhadrāvudha and Gotama of Āḷavī too—
so too you should commit to faith.
You will go, Piṅgiya, beyond the domain of death.”

5.19.s:
“Esa bhiyyo pasīdāmi,
Sutvāna munino vaco;
Vivaṭṭacchado sambuddho,
Akhilo paṭibhānavā.
5.19.e:
“My confidence grows
as I hear the word of the sage,
the Buddha with veil cast off,
so kind and eloquent.

5.19.s:
Adhideve abhiññāya,
Sabbaṁ vedi varovaraṁ;
Pañhānantakaro satthā,
Kaṅkhīnaṁ paṭijānataṁ.
5.19.e:
Having directly known all about the gods,
he understands all top to bottom,
the Teacher who settles all questions
for those who admit their doubts.

5.19.s:
Asaṁhīraṁ asaṅkuppaṁ,
Yassa natthi upamā kvaci;
Addhā gamissāmi na mettha kaṅkhā,
Evaṁ maṁ dhārehi adhimuttacittan”ti.
5.19.e:
The unfaltering, the unshakable:
that to which there is no compare.
For sure I will go there, I have no doubt of that.
Remember me as one whose mind is made up.”

5.19.s:
Paṭhamakaṭṭhavaro varavaggo,
Dvādasasuttadharo suvibhatto;
Desito cakkhumatā vimalena,
Suyyati vaggavaro uragoti.

Ratanāmagandho hirimaṅgalanāmo,
Sucilomakapilo ca brāhmaṇadhammo;
Nāvā kiṁsīlauṭṭhahano ca,
Rāhulo ca punapi vaṅgīso.

Sammāparibbājanīyopi cettha,
Dhammikasuttavaro suvibhatto;
Cuddasasuttadharo dutiyamhi,
Cūḷakavaggavaroti tamāhu.

Pabbajjapadhānasubhāsitanāmo,
Pūraḷāso punadeva māgho ca;
Sabhiyaṁ keṇiyameva sallanāmo,
Vāseṭṭhavaro kālikopi ca.

Nālakasuttavaro suvibhatto,
Taṁ anupassī tathā punadeva;
Dvādasasuttadharo tatiyamhi,
Suyyati vaggavaro mahānāmo.

Kāmaguhaṭṭhakaduṭṭhakanāmā,
Suddhavaro paramaṭṭhakanāmo;
Jarā mettiyavaro suvibhatto,
Pasūramāgaṇḍiyā purābhedo.

Kalahavivādo ubho viyuhā ca,
Tuvaṭakaattadaṇḍasāriputtā;
Soḷasasuttadharo catutthamhi,
Aṭṭhakavaggavaroti tamāhu.

Magadhe janapade ramaṇīye,
Desavare katapuññanivese;
Pāsāṇakacetiyavare suvibhatte,
Vasi bhagavā gaṇaseṭṭho.

Byañjanamatthapadaṁ samayuttaṁ,
Akkharasaññitaopamagāḷhaṁ;
Lokavicāraṇañāṇapabhaggaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Klesamale amalaṁ vimalaggaṁ,
Duccaritamale amalaṁ vimalaggaṁ;
Lokavicāraṇañāṇapabhaggaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Āsavabandhanayogākilesaṁ,
Nīvaraṇāni ca tīṇi malāni;
Tassa kilesapamocanahetuṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Nimmalasabbakilesapanūdaṁ,
Rāgavirāgamanejamasokaṁ;
Santapaṇītasududdasadhammaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Rāgañca dosakamabhañjitasantaṁ,
Yonicatuggatipañcaviññāṇaṁ;
Taṇhāratacchadanatāṇalatāpamokkhaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Gambhīraduddasasaṇhanipuṇaṁ,
Paṇḍitavedaniyaṁ nipuṇatthaṁ;
Lokavicāraṇañāṇapabhaggaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Navaṅgakusumamālagīveyyaṁ,
Indriyajhānavimokkhavibhattaṁ;
Aṭṭhaṅgamaggadharaṁ varayānaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Somupamaṁ vimalaṁ parisuddhaṁ,
Aṇṇavamūpamaratanasucittaṁ;
Pupphasamaṁ ravimūpamatejaṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggo.

Khemasivaṁ sukhasītalasantaṁ,
Maccutatāṇaparaṁ paramatthaṁ;
Tassa sunibbutadassanahetuṁ,
Desayi suttavaraṁ dvipadaggoti.
